scenes.say: Ever wondered how Docker containers find each other, or how ports get mapped? Let's break it down.

scenes.label: Bridge
scenes.sub: Each container gets a private IP on the bridge network.
scenes.say: By default, Docker gives each container its own private address on a bridge network.

rows.b: docker run with appnet, name db
docker run with appnet, name api
by using db as the host name

scenes.say: With your own networks, containers can find each other by name. The API can reach the database just by using its name.

scenes.title: Publish a port
scenes.say: To let outside traffic in, publish a port. Here, host port eighty eighty connects to container port eight thousand.

scenes.question: What does -p 8080:8000 do?
scenes.wrong: It exposes port 8080 inside the container.
scenes.right: It connects host port eighty eighty to container port eight thousand.
scenes.say: Watch out: publishing a port links the host and container ports, not just exposes a port inside the container.
